description: I am a developer building 'AuraHealth Astro' for the Astronaut Health Monitoring challenge. I have designed the core architecture with a telemetry backend and a mission-ready dashboard interface. Looking for teammates interested in domain research, NASA open data analysis, or presentation to collaborate and submit a complete solution together!
summary: AuraHealth Astro is an offline-first, delay-tolerant astronaut health intelligence and environmental telemetry console aligned with NASA-STD-3001. During deep-space missions to the Moon or Mars, Earth communication blackouts of up to 20 minutes (1,200 seconds) prevent real-time ground medical intervention. AuraHealth Astro solves this by running a local Python/FastAPI clinical rule engine and Flutter desktop console directly inside the habitat, delivering 0 ms local alert latency across multi-crew vitals (heart rate, SpO2, core temperature, blood pressure) and cabin environmental thresholds (PCO2 <= 3.0 mmHg). Every telemetry record is persisted in an append-only SQLite WAL store-and-forward outbox signed with deterministic RFC 8785 canonical JSON SHA-256 receipts, guaranteeing 0% data loss when simulated Earth relay links drop. Integrating live NASA DONKI space weather alongside NASA OSDR, CSA, and ESA open-science baselines, it protects crews beyond low-Earth orbit and adapts directly to disconnected rural clinics on Earth.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

AuraHealth Astro is a local-first spaceflight health monitoring and telemetry verification platform engineered for deep-space habitats experiencing severe Earth-link latency and communication blackouts. Built with a Python 3.14 / FastAPI backend, SQLite Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) persistence, and a Flutter Windows desktop mission console, the system continuously ingests multi-crew physiological telemetry (heart rate, SpO2, core body temperature, systolic/diastolic blood pressure) alongside cabin atmospheric metrics (cabin PCO2). Whenever vitals deviate from individual crew baselines or breach NASA-STD-3001 safety thresholds (such as cabin PCO2 exceeding 3.0 mmHg), the onboard clinical rule engine triggers immediate 0 ms local alerts with actionable Flight Surgeon protocol guidance—requiring zero internet connectivity.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact:

1. Zero Telemetry Loss Under Blackouts: An append-only SQLite WAL outbox queues all clinical events locally during 20-minute (1,200s) simulated deep-space blackouts and automatically flushes acknowledgments once the Earth relay reconnects.

2. Cryptographic Auditability: Every ingested telemetry packet is canonicalized using RFC 8785 and hashed with SHA-256 to generate tamper-evident mission receipts.

3. Dual Space & Terrestrial Impact: Beyond protecting Artemis and Mars transit crews, the exact offline-first architecture serves remote clinics, disaster zones, and low-connectivity healthcare facilities on Earth.

Tools, Languages & Verification:

- Backend & Persistence: Python 3.14, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLite (WAL mode), RFC 8785 canonicalization.

- Frontend Console: Flutter / Dart desktop UI featuring live trend charts, crew profile switching, Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) wellness logging, and an interactive Earth Relay latency simulator.

- Engineering Validation: Verified with 125/125 passing automated backend unit tests and 0 Flutter static analysis issues. All biosignal and relay streams are clearly labeled as simulated telemetry for demonstration integrity.

Creativity & Team Execution:

Combining deterministic cryptographic receipts with an interactive deep-space blackout simulator allows mission controllers and crew members to test autonomous medical triage under realistic delay conditions. Team roles were structured across lead systems architecture and full-stack development (Bijoy Mojumder), presentation and documentation support (Nazia Titim), and usability review and coordination (Md Abdul Rahim Parosh).
